text:
emma (support): Escalating CloudMesa onboarding — customer can't finish dataset upload and the provisioner returns 403 when creating their dedicated workspace. Renewal in ~18 days; customer said onboarding delay may affect purchase. Marking P0.
rachel (cs): Acknowledged. Can you paste the error and any request ids/screenshots?
emma (support): UI shows `Upload failed: row 42: invalid mapping` for CSV import. Separately the provision API returns 403 with request id prov-cc9. Screenshot attached. They also reported their IPs are allowlisted on their side.
rachel (cs): Assigning @tom to triage the 403+ingest engine. I'll own customer comms and loop in @jules if renewal risk rises.
tom (eng): Quick look: ingest pipeline rejects files when the CSV has mixed schema (datetime in col expected int). We'll add a pre-validate step. Provision 403 is because the workspace creation call originates from an internal worker IP that's not in customer's allowlist (worker pool shifted after last deploy). Triggering a short infra patch to route through the public egress IP. Running fix: `scripts/egress-fix --pool=onboard-workers --target-ip=34.82.11.5`
infra-bot: egress-fix job started (job-id: ef-2141) for pool onboard-workers
emma (support): After egress fix, provision attempts returned 200 for new requests; customer still sees some rows failing on re-upload.
tom (eng): For CSVs: I'm deploying a simple validator that returns clearer errors and auto-casts common date formats. Command: `kubectl apply -f validators/pre-validate.yaml` — will also run a repair to reprocess accepted rows.
rachel (cs): Drafting customer message: "Hi Sam — thank you for the patience. We found two issues: (1) some rows in your CSV used a datetime format our importer didn't accept; we fixed the importer to validate and auto-cast common formats and reprocessed your successful rows, and (2) workspace creation was blocked by your IP allowlist because our onboarding worker egress IP rotated; we routed provisioning through your allowlisted IP and provisioning now succeeds. Please retry the upload and we'll monitor for 24 hours. We can also schedule a 1-hour enablement call and offer a 2-week trial extension if you'd like." Sending now.
jules (sales): Noted — CloudMesa is in pilot-to-paid cadence. If onboarding slips, offer the extension and priority enablement to keep them.
anya (solutions): I'll schedule the enablement call and prepare a short checklist to avoid CSV formatting issues.
tom (eng): Reprocessing job finished; logs show rows 1-410 processed OK, rows with invalid dates failed with explicit errors now. I'll add a follow-up ticket to improve importer docs.
emma (support): Customer reply: "Uploads succeeded after the fix; workspace created. Appreciate the quick turnaround." (reply arrived ~30m after fixes)
rachel (cs): Updated CRM: onboarding -> "Completed", renewal_risk -> "Cleared". Note: offered 2-week extension and enablement; customer accepted enablement, declined extension. Captured feedback: improve importer error messages.
tom (eng): Leaving monitoring for 3 hours on ingest-worker and provisioner: `journalctl -u ingest-worker -f` and `journalctl -u provisioner -f` with alert on any 403 spikes.
rachel (cs): Closing escalation. Actions: Anya schedule enablement, Tom add importer docs ticket + 3h monitoring, Emma watch support alerts, Rachel notify renewal lead and sales. Thanks team :tada:
